5. // Imports

8. use vstd::prelude::*;
9. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
10. include!("number.spec.rs");
11. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
12. include!("number.proof.rs");
13. 
14. use crate::mem;
15. 
16. //==================================================================================================
17. // Structures
18. //==================================================================================================
19. 
20. ///
21. /// # Description
22. ///
23. /// A type that represents a frame number.
24. /// A frame number is in the range from `0` to [`Self::MAX`] (inclusive).
25. ///
26. #[verus_verify]
27. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
28. pub struct FrameNumber(usize);
29. 
30. //==================================================================================================
31. // Implementations
32. //==================================================================================================
33. 
34. #[verus_verify]
35. impl FrameNumber {
36.     /// The maximum frame number.
37.     pub const MAX: usize = mem::MAX_ADDRESS / mem::FRAME_SIZE - 1;
38. 
39.     #[verus_spec(ensures Self::NULL@ == 0)]
40.     pub const NULL: Self = Self(0);
41. 
42.     ///
43.     /// # Description
44.     ///
45.     /// Constructs a [`FrameNumber`].
46.     ///
47.     /// # Parameters
48.     ///
49.     /// - `value`: The value of the frame number.
50.     ///
51.     /// # Returns
52.     ///
53.     /// - `Some(`[`FrameNumber`]`)`: Upon success.
54.     /// - `None`: If the value is greater than [`Self::MAX`].
55.     ///
56.     #[verus_spec(result =>
57.         ensures
58.             value as int <= Self::spec_max() ==> (result is Some
59.                 && (result->Some_0)@ == value as int),
60.             value as int > Self::spec_max() ==> result is None,
61.     )]
62.     pub fn from_raw_value(value: usize) -> Option<Self> {
63.         if value > Self::MAX {
64.             return None;
65.         }
66. 
67.         Some(Self(value))
68.     }
69. 
70.     ///
71.     /// # Description
72.     ///
73.     /// Converts a [`FrameNumber`] into a raw value.
74.     ///
75.     /// # Returns
76.     ///
77.     /// The raw value of the target [`FrameNumber`].
78.     ///
79.     #[verus_spec(result =>
80.         ensures
81.             result as int == self@,
82.             0 <= self@ <= Self::spec_max(),
83.     )]
84.     pub fn into_raw_value(self) -> usize {
85.         proof! { use_type_invariant(self); }
86.         self.0
87.     }
88. }
89. 
90. //==================================================================================================
91. // Unit Tests
92. //==================================================================================================
93. 
94. /// Tests if [`FrameNumber::from_raw_value()`] successfully constructs frame zero.
95. #[test]
96. fn test_frame_number_from_raw_value_zero() {
97.     let raw_value: usize = 0;
98.     let frame_number: FrameNumber = FrameNumber::from_raw_value(raw_value).unwrap();
99.     assert_eq!(frame_number.into_raw_value(), raw_value);
100. }
101. 
102. /// Tests if [`FrameNumber::from_raw_value()`] successfully constructs the maximum frame number.
103. #[test]
104. fn test_frame_number_from_raw_value_max() {
105.     let raw_value: usize = FrameNumber::MAX;
106.     let frame_number: FrameNumber = FrameNumber::from_raw_value(raw_value).unwrap();
107.     assert_eq!(frame_number.into_raw_value(), raw_value);
108. }

2. 
3. //==================================================================================================
4. // View
5. //==================================================================================================
6. 
7. impl View for FrameNumber {
8.     type V = int;
9. 
10.     // `closed`: callers reference `self@`, but the mapping to the inner `usize` field is hidden.
11.     // The abstract value is "the frame index as int". Realizes the kernel's uninterpreted
12.     // `spec_frame_raw_value(frame)`.
13.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int {
14.         self.0 as int
15.     }
16. }
17. 
18. //==================================================================================================
19. // Abstract bound + type invariant
20. //==================================================================================================
21. 
22. impl FrameNumber {
23.     // Interpreted bound: the largest representable frame index, mirroring the exec constant
24.     // `FrameNumber::MAX = MAX_ADDRESS / FRAME_SIZE - 1`. Defined (not `uninterp`) so the binding to
25.     // `MAX` is discharged by verification rather than assumed. Realizes the kernel's
26.     // `spec_max_frame_number()` (see `hal/mem/types/address/phys.spec.rs`). The `nat` result makes
27.     // the bound non-negative for callers (e.g. constructing `FrameNumber::NULL`).
28.     pub open spec fn spec_max() -> nat {
29.         (mem::MAX_ADDRESS / mem::FRAME_SIZE - 1) as nat
30.     }
31. 
32.     // Every constructible `FrameNumber` is bounded by `MAX`. Enforced as a type invariant so the
33.     // bound holds unconditionally for any value callers hold (PTE/PDE treat it as an always-valid
34.     // token), which is exactly what lets `into_raw_value() << FRAME_SHIFT` not overflow `usize`.
35.     #[verifier::type_invariant]
36.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
37.         0 <= self@ <= Self::spec_max()
38.     }
39. }
40. 
41. } // verus!
